title: Establish token override surface hierarchy for icon and split buttons
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Icon buttons and split (compound) buttons are increasingly customized by product teams using ad-hoc token overrides. Without a clear override surface and hierarchy, teams accidentally create inconsistencies across density, focus states, and loading affordances. This ticket defines a predictable token override model and surface hierarchy so designers and engineers can safely customize appearance without regressing accessibility or spacing.
goals: Define a minimal override surface (surface, outline, icon-size, padding, spinner-size, press-depth) for icon / split buttons
Document token inheritance and the precedence rules (component defaults < variant presets < theme overrides < explicit per-instance tokens)
Provide migration guidelines for existing overrides and a runtime-safe CSS var fallback strategy
Preserve accessibility (hit target, focus ring contrast, reduced-motion, high-contrast) across overrides
Ship design tokens JSON, Figma styles, and a reference implementation in the UI-kit
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with explicit token names and example permutations (icon-only, icon+label, split primary/secondary) published in Confluence
Figma component library updated with recommended tokens attached to each instance and a short comment explaining override precedence
UI-kit PR implementing token lookup and CSS var fallback merged with unit tests covering RTL and reduced-motion
QA checklist passed: keyboard focus, touch hitbox, spinner alignment, label truncation, and density toggles
Migration note added to release notes and a short codemod suggested for large repos
engineering_notes: Key runtime constraints: theme switches happen at root, per-instance tokens should be applied via CSS vars to avoid rerendering React trees
Prefer a flattening algorithm that resolves values in this order: component default -> variant preset -> theme override -> per-instance explicit token
Spinner sizing must snap to icon-size token when present; fallback to computed font-size if undefined
Edge case: split-button separators must remain touchable at 44px regardless of padding overrides (enforce min-hit pixels)
Implementation spike: create a small util in ui-kit that resolves token keys to computed CSS variables and expose a TS type for allowed override keys
tradeoffs_and_risks: Making too many override keys increases surface area for inconsistency; we limit the surface to 7 keys to reduce cognitive load
Runtime CSS var strategy adds some complexity for older browsers; fallback will use inline styles applied by the component as a last resort
Automated codemod may miss hand-tuned instances; we will include a manual review step for high-traffic screens
design_decisions: Mapping: icon-size drives spinner-size by default (spinner-size = ceil(icon-size * 0.9))
Min hit target enforcement is a component-level rule and not part of token overrides
High-contrast and reduced-motion will ignore per-instance motion tokens unless explicitly allowed by label 'allow-motion-overrides'
qa_steps: 1) Verify all permutations in the playground: icon-only (small/medium/large), icon+label, split primary/secondary
2) Toggle theme overrides and confirm precedence rules visually and via computed CSS variables
3) Keyboard navigation: ensure focus ring is visible and meets contrast requirements
4) Touch test on mobile: ensure separators and icon hit targets are >=44px where applicable
5) Run automated accessibility scan and smoke test storybook snapshots for regressions
